claims.proposition: A declared spending constraint should be represented explicitly during evaluation instead of being inferred only from a global linear price penalty.

scope.population: Consumers making constrained discrete choices; lodging transfer remains methodological

limits: No hotel-specific coefficient or threshold is supported
nonApplicableWhen: The user has not supplied or implied a defensible budget constraint

claims.proposition: Price, hotel rating, location and cancellation conditions can all influence online hotel choice, but their relative importance is sample- and period-dependent.

scope.population: United States online hotel shoppers in a stated-choice study

limits: The study does not license universal weights or post-pandemic extrapolation
nonApplicableWhen: The booking context or population materially differs and no local validation exists

claims.proposition: A positive review score should be interpreted with its review-volume context rather than treated as equally credible at every volume.

scope.population: Participants in a controlled hotel consideration experiment

limits: Volume informs credibility context and is not itself evidence of superior stay quality
nonApplicableWhen: The platform does not expose a comparable, deduplicated review count

claims.proposition: Official star classification and guest review evidence are non-interchangeable quality signals and must retain separate provenance.

scope.population: Dubai hotels and online customer review data

limits: Classification systems and review platforms differ across markets
nonApplicableWhen: Either source signal lacks provenance or uses an undocumented scale

claims.proposition: The importance of value, location, sleep, room, cleanliness and service can differ across hotel segments and rating contexts.

scope.population: Consumers evaluating four United States chain brands

limits: Exploratory four-brand results require replication before policy use
nonApplicableWhen: A segment or classification is not comparable to the studied brands

claims.proposition: Room and comfort importance varies with trip purpose, traveler type and travel companions; sleep quality is recurrent but not a universal complete comfort vector.

scope.population: Finnish residents reporting leisure and work-related hotel stays

limits: Qualitative evidence identifies themes but cannot estimate scoring weights
nonApplicableWhen: The traveler has supplied explicit preferences that contradict aggregate themes

claims.proposition: Trip purpose can moderate hotel attribute trade-offs, so business and leisure labels should be treated as context signals rather than fixed preference assignments.

scope.population: Participants in solo-business and family-leisure stated scenarios

limits: Scenario averages must yield to explicit traveler preferences
nonApplicableWhen: The trip label is unknown, mixed-purpose or contradicted by explicit preferences

claims.proposition: Location evaluation should preserve trip-specific walking time, neighborhood and points of interest rather than collapse every destination into one generic distance signal.

scope.population: Tourists evaluating Hong Kong hotel locations

limits: Relevant points of interest and transport modes differ by destination and traveler
nonApplicableWhen: No trip-specific destination anchors or defensible travel-time evidence exist

claims.proposition: Regret-sensitive comparison is a research candidate for location trade-offs, but one destination study cannot establish it as the default decision rule.

scope.population: Tourists evaluating Hong Kong hotel locations

limits: Model fit in one stated-choice study does not prove global behavioral superiority
nonApplicableWhen: No pairwise regret hypothesis is under explicit offline evaluation

claims.proposition: Room attributes and cancellation conditions can carry value, but their willingness-to-pay estimates are property-, segment- and trip-context-dependent.

scope.population: Guests in a single-property discrete-choice study

limits: No study estimate becomes a universal upgrade price or room score
nonApplicableWhen: The room attribute is unavailable, ambiguously described or not comparable

claims.proposition: The value of cancellation and date-change conditions can increase with the booking window and should not be represented by one context-free premium.

scope.population: Guests interviewed in three Netherlands chain properties

limits: The observed willingness-to-pay values are not portable thresholds
nonApplicableWhen: Lead time is unknown or the rate conditions are not reliably parsed

claims.proposition: Kitchen, amenities, residential feel, cost efficiency, minimum-stay rules and review availability are candidate long-stay capabilities for further validation.
limits: Industry evidence with unknown public sample size cannot define weights or represent other traveler populations
nonApplicableWhen: The stay is shorter than five days or the traveler is outside the studied business-travel population

claims.proposition: Cross-country differences in rating levels and satisfaction drivers make an unvalidated global review mean unsafe as a universal quality norm.

scope.population: Hotel guests represented in an eight-country satisfaction analysis

limits: Institutional aggregate satisfaction evidence is contextual and non-causal
nonApplicableWhen: A locally validated, platform-specific normalization already exists for the target population

testMappings.assertion: Budget-sensitive cases distinguish a hard affordability constraint from a context-free linear price penalty.
Equivalent options can change role or ordering only when explicit trip, party or segment context changes.
A global raw review mean cannot enter policy without local platform and geography validation.
Matched cases test whether longer lead time can increase the value of equivalent cancellation protection without fixing a universal premium.
Location cases use traveler-relevant anchors and travel time, including accessibility constraints, instead of generic center distance alone.
Long-stay capabilities remain explicit contextual facts and no industry percentage is converted into a global weight.
Regret-sensitive behavior is evaluated offline against additive utility and cannot become the global default from one study.
Matched review scores with materially different evidence volume remain distinguishable in reliability context.
Room and comfort cases vary party, purpose and explicit preferences without importing a universal willingness-to-pay coefficient.
Official classification and guest review evidence retain separate fields, scales and provenance.

biasControls.risk: Walking time, room comfort and convenience can exclude mobility, sensory or cognitive access needs.
biasControls.mitigation: Require accessibility constraints and compatible transport or room facts before applying generic location or comfort assumptions.
biasControls.requiredReview: Include accessibility adversarial cases and a reviewer with accessibility-domain competence.

biasControls.risk: Country-specific samples and rating norms can be mistaken for universal traveler behavior.
biasControls.mitigation: Preserve geography scope, prohibit global coefficients and require local replication before policy candidacy.
biasControls.requiredReview: Compare at least two materially different geographies before any normalization proposal.

biasControls.risk: Chain, star class, extended-stay and independent properties expose different attributes and expectations.
biasControls.mitigation: Tag segment explicitly and prohibit transfer when the target property class is not represented.
biasControls.requiredReview: Stratify validation cases by property segment and classification regime.

biasControls.risk: Stars, scores, volumes, badges and displayed rate conditions can use incompatible scales or collection rules.
biasControls.mitigation: Retain source provenance and scale metadata; never substitute one signal for another silently.
biasControls.requiredReview: Run schema and provenance tests for every platform-derived signal.

biasControls.risk: Pandemic conditions, inflation, platform redesign and changing cancellation norms can age evidence quickly.
biasControls.mitigation: Enforce review-by dates and downgrade or retire claims when context has materially changed.
biasControls.requiredReview: Re-run temporal relevance review at each claim review-by date.

biasControls.risk: Solo travelers, couples, families and groups have materially different room and convenience constraints.
biasControls.mitigation: Keep party composition explicit and let declared needs override population averages.
biasControls.requiredReview: Include solo, couple, child, group and multi-room cases in the curriculum.

biasControls.risk: Business and leisure averages can become stereotypes and erase mixed-purpose trips.
biasControls.mitigation: Treat purpose as defeasible context, preserve mixed and unknown states, and prioritize explicit preferences.
biasControls.requiredReview: Test business, leisure, mixed and unknown purpose without fixed role assignment.
